name: Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9)
instructions: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?

items.text: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed? Or the opposite — being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way

functionalItem.text: If you checked off any problems, how difficult have these problems made it for you to do your work, take care of things at home, or get along with other people?

bands.label: None-minimal
bands.clinicianNote: Total falls in the none-to-minimal range. A low total does not rule out a mood concern, so consider it alongside the interview and history; clinical judgment decides.

bands.label: Mild
bands.clinicianNote: Total falls in the mild range. Consider watchful monitoring and repeating the questionnaire over time to see the trend; clinical judgment decides.

bands.label: Moderate
bands.clinicianNote: Total falls in the moderate range. A total of 10 or more is the commonly cited cutoff that calls for further evaluation, so consider a fuller assessment and a discussion of care options; clinical judgment decides.

bands.label: Moderately severe
bands.clinicianNote: Total falls in the moderately severe range. Consider a timely, thorough assessment and an active discussion of care options with the client; clinical judgment decides.

bands.label: Severe
bands.clinicianNote: Total falls in the severe range. Consider a prompt, thorough assessment, a discussion of care options and whether a medical or psychiatric consultation would help; clinical judgment decides.

riskItems.message: Item 9 answered above "Not at all": follow up directly with a suicide-risk assessment (for example, the C-SSRS) and safety planning, guided by your clinical judgment and local protocol. This app does not assess or decide risk.

citation: Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JBW. The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure. J Gen Intern Med. 2001;16(9):606-613.
